decisive_items: Four hours post-procedure, the patient experienced intermittent abdominal pain and occasional nausea.
Ascites culture yielded growth of Escherichia coli.
Bacterial colonies observed in submucosa surrounding the ESD lesion.
response.rationale: Post-procedure onset, peritonism, E. coli ascites, and bacterial colonies around the ESD lesion localize the illness to a procedure-related peritonitis; infectious colitis is the nearest alternative but lacks the procedural/peritoneal link.

rejected.why: CT shows no perforation and no diverticula; findings center on the ascending colon/ESD site.
No true neutropenia; abscesses and neutrophils argue against neutropenic typhlitis.
No appendiceal findings and CT explicitly excludes intestinal perforation.
Sepsis is a downstream systemic label; local peritonitis with E. coli ascites is the primary diagnosis.
Absolute neutrophil count is not severely low and histology shows neutrophilic abscesses, not neutropenic colitis.
Right-sided pain overlaps, but imaging and histology point to the ascending colon around the ESD lesion, not the appendix.
